# Text critique and suggestions — Astralis Tarot

Companion to `UX_FLAWS.md`. Everything here is about words: what the app says, whether it is true, and whether it is any good.

Sample output quoted below is real: every reader was run against The Tower (upright), Five of Cups (reversed) and King of Pentacles (upright) with the question "should I quit my job?".

**Before editing:** `js/cards.js` is generated by `build_cards_data.js`. Card copy must be changed in the generator (or the generator retired), or the edits will be overwritten. See UX-160.

---

## Verdict

1. **Three voices are fighting for the interface.** Gothic-mystic ("The Oracle's Light", "Sacred Ten", "active vortex of energy"), Cassian's print shop ("Turn the plate", "The case", "the clerk"), and plain functional ("Copy link", "Shuffle & deal"). The chrome should be the plain one. Personality belongs to the readers.
2. **Four of the seven readers are mad-libs.** Vivienne, Corvus, Aurelius and Celeste splice a sentence fragment from the card data into a fixed template. The output is ungrammatical, identical in structure every time, and often nonsense. They are prototype scaffolding next to three readers that were actually written.
3. **The three written readers (Ruth, Cassian, Lyle) are good and are being worn out by repetition.** Fixed openers, fixed closers, and running gags that appear in every reading.
4. **The card data describes pictures where it should give meanings**, and those pictures are not the ones on screen.

---

## 2. The four template readers: cut or rewrite

**TXT-030 · Recommendation: remove Madame Vivienne, Corvus Thorne, Dr. Aurelius and Celeste Nova, or rewrite each with per-card lines to the standard of the other three.** What follows is why.

They all work the same way: take `card.meaningUpright` (a fragment, often starting with a capital and containing no verb) and drop it mid-sentence into fixed scaffolding.

**Madame Vivienne** — actual output:

> "King of Pentacles (Upright) emerges in the sanctuary of The Future / Horizon. With the elemental pulse of Earth, Prosperous lord seated in grape-rich stone castle with bull heads carved in relief; enterprise mastery, steady abundance, generative security. The thread of destiny emphasizes Generative Abundance, Business Mastery, Steadfast Security."

- "With the elemental pulse of Earth, Prosperous lord seated…" is not a sentence.
- "(Upright)" repeats the chip beside it.
- "The thread of destiny emphasizes" followed by three Title Case keywords is a database dump with incense on it.
- The advice always names the first card ("Honor The Tower's lesson before taking another step") whatever its position.
- The advice and the blessing are the same two sentences in every reading, forever.
- "The Minor Arcana dominate your reading" appears with a Major on the table (UX-007).

**Corvus Thorne** — actual output:

> "Position [The Past / Origin]: Even upright, The Tower demands scrutiny. The ego may identify too strongly with this posture. Are you hiding behind sudden upheaval as a defense? Notice how this intersects with: "Cataclysmic breakthrough, shattering of illusions…""

- "Position [ … ]:" is debug formatting.
- "Are you hiding behind *sudden upheaval* as a defense?" and "running from *acceptance*" are what the template produces when the keyword does not fit. It rarely fits.
- "You have 1 reversed card(s)".
- His "philosophy" is the line commonly attributed to Jung, presented in quotation marks as his own.
- Every upright card gets the same three sentences; every reversed card gets the same one.

**Dr. Aurelius** — actual output:

> "Mitigation Step: Eliminate inefficiencies caused by Five of Cups (Acceptance). Turning around to see what remains, emotional recovery, forgiveness… Identify the specific bottleneck and pause non-essential expenditures of energy."

- "Allocate 70% of your focus to developing this asset" is appended to every upright card. Two upright cards is 140%.
- "Eliminate inefficiencies caused by Five of Cups (Acceptance)" is meaningless.
- "The system exhibits strong Fire variance" misuses "variance".
- The advice refers to "the crossing or obstacle card" in spreads that have neither.
- A consultant parody can work. This one has no jokes, only vocabulary.

**Celeste Nova** — actual output:

> "House [The Past / Origin]: Governed by The Tower (Direct Transit — Harmonious Trine / Conjunction). Resonating with Fire / Mars. … Esoteric vibration: "Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty"."

- Every upright card is a "Harmonious Trine / Conjunction" and every reversed card a "Hard Square / Opposition". These are relationships between two bodies; assigning one to a single card is astrological nonsense that anyone who knows the subject will spot at once.
- "Planetary retrogrades and alignments emphasize timing, patience, and aligning with larger astrological cycles" says nothing.
- "Track the current moon phase tonight" is the advice for every reading.

**All four:** titles are double epithets joined by an ampersand ("The Mystic Seer & High Oracle", "The Shadow Oracle & Jungian Inquisitor", "The Pragmatic Alchemist & Strategist", "The Cosmic Astrologer & Stargazer"). One each.

## 3. The three written readers: good, and over-seasoned

### Ruth Calloway

Best voice-to-length ratio in the app: about 38 words a card, one image each, no filler. Keep the card lines.

- **TXT-040** · `"You asked: "should I quit my job?." Alright, hon…"` — a full stop is added after the user's own punctuation (`ruth-calloway.js:441`). Strip trailing punctuation or drop the period.
- **TXT-041** · "hon" appears 28 times in the file and is in the fixed opener and fixed closer. In one reading it lands three or four times. Take it out of the fixed lines so it only arrives with a card.
- **TXT-042** · The biography does not add up. Bio: "Thirty-one years behind the wheel". Backstory: licence at nineteen, sixty-one now, parked "four years back". That is thirty-eight years.
- **TXT-043** · Name `Ruth "Roadhouse" Calloway` and title "The Long-Haul Oracle of the Blue Star Truck Stop" are both too long for the header chip and reader card. "Ruth Calloway" / "Blue Star Truck Stop, I-40".
- Missing frames for six positions (UX-005) must be written: situation, obstacle, advice, mind, body, spirit.
- The tally line says "Fire / Water / Air / Earth" from a reader whose premise is "no energy, no universe". Use suits or road terms.

### Cassian Vetch

The writing in the first half of each card is the strongest in the repository ("The chain is loose enough to lift, and you have decided it is jewelry."). The second half undoes it.

- **TXT-045** · Every one of the 156 card lines ends with the same three-part rig: "The picture in the case is … The stake is … Stamp: …". The first two restate what was just said, in the same words each time. A Celtic Cross runs to about 1,030 words of card text and shows that scaffold ten times. **Cut "The picture in the case is" and "The stake is" from all 156 lines. Keep the Stamp.** That alone removes about a quarter of the length.
- **TXT-046** · The bio in the reader list is about 100 words, three times anyone else's. Two sentences.
- **TXT-047** · `philosophy: "He stamps the sentence you were avoiding."` is third person, and the drawer wraps it in quotation marks as though he said it. Make it his: "I stamp the sentence you were avoiding."
- **TXT-048** · Fixed opener "Slip received. I am reading it the way it came in: "…"." has the same doubled punctuation as Ruth's, and the fixed closer ("…then I have a condolence card to lock up") is charming once and a tic by the third reading. Write three or four closers and vary them.
- **TXT-049** · Orientation label "Slipped plate" replaces "Reversed" (UX-006). Good phrase, wrong place; move it into the prose, where "printed upside down" already does the job.
- **TXT-050** · Position frame, crossing card: "A second plate, printing over the true impression you actually set:" — "true" and "actually" are both doing the same work. "A second plate, printed over the one you set:".

### Lyle Pasternak

The "Slip" lines are the funniest writing here ("A new beginning is available. So is gravity."). The framing around them is the problem.

- **TXT-044** · The score: "Score: I don't do scores until you stop explaining. Fine. 5 out of 10, and I'm being generous because the Slim Jim was good." Identical wording every reading, and the number can only be 1–6 (UX-012). Either write a set of score lines keyed to the result or drop the score.
- **TXT-051** · Props are over-used: Doris, the laminator, the Slim Jim and the Circuit City sign appear 21 times across his files and in the bio, the opener, the score and the closer. Each can appear in the fixed text once at most; let the card lines carry the rest.
- **TXT-052** · "Contestant" and "pal" are in the fixed opener for every reading. Same treatment.
- **TXT-053** · Orientation labels "Upright, unfortunately" and "Face-down in the dip" (UX-006). The first is printed on every upright card, so a ten-card spread says "unfortunately" up to ten times.
- **TXT-054** · `alias: "Don't"` and `style: "unhinged"` are metadata jokes nobody sees. Fine; just don't surface `style` in the interface.

## 4. Spread and position copy (`js/spreads.js`, `app.js:453–465`)

Position names appear on small tags above the cards, in the reading list, and in screen-reader labels. Descriptions appear only as hover tooltips.

- **TXT-060** · Names with slashes: "The Past / Origin", "The Present / Nexus", "The Future / Horizon", "The Foundation / Root". The code strips "The" for the tag, leaving "PAST / ORIGIN" in tiny caps. Nobody needs the second half. → "Past", "Present", "Future", "Root".
- **TXT-061** · Celtic Cross names are costume: "The Crowning Mind", "The Seeker's Self", "The External Realm", "The Passing Past", "The Near Horizon", "The Crossing Force". → "Present", "Challenge", "Root", "Recent past", "Aim", "Near future", "You", "Others", "Hopes and fears", "Outcome".
- **TXT-062** · Subtitles repeat the name in longer words: "Core Essence & Focal Guidance", "Foundations & Root Causes", "Synthesis & Culmination", "The Secret Threshold". Each row in the reading shows name and subtitle together. Delete the subtitles or make each a plain gloss ("what is leaving").
- **TXT-063** · Descriptions are the worst prose in the project:
  - "The active vortex of energy, your present state of mind, and the immediate dynamics at play."
  - "Past experiences, karmic conditioning, and foundational influences that shaped where you stand now."
  - "The grand resolution; the harmonic synthesis of all previous nine cards when integrated."
  - "Somatic energy, health, work, and tangible life."
  - "Soul calling, intuition, and cosmic alignment."
  - "The optimal strategy and mindful posture."

  Lists of three abstractions, none of which helps a person read a card. One plain sentence each: "What is happening now." "Where this is likely to end up if nothing changes."
- **TXT-064** · Spread descriptions: "The revered ten-card divination mandala revealing the subconscious root, crowning conscious will, surrounding forces, and ultimate outcome." → "Ten cards: the situation, what crosses it, what lies behind and ahead, and where it leads." The three-card one is also wrong for two frames (UX-004).
- **TXT-065** · Position single card: "The Guiding Light — Core Essence & Focal Guidance". → "Your card".

## 5. Card data (`build_cards_data.js` → `js/cards.js`)

- **TXT-070** · **Minor-card "meanings" are picture descriptions with keywords attached.** "Prosperous lord seated in grape-rich stone castle with bull heads carved in relief; enterprise mastery, steady abundance, generative security." "Bandaged warrior leaning on protective staff; bruised but resilient, guarding final line of defense." "Fiery charger galloping through desert sands; fearless audacity…". They describe Rider–Waite scenes, which the default cat deck does not show; they have no verb; and four readers quote them mid-sentence. Rewrite all 112 minor meanings as one or two full sentences about what the card means.
- **TXT-071** · Dropped articles throughout, telegram style: "letting go of unchangeable past", "guarding final line of defense", "seated in grape-rich stone castle".
- **TXT-072** · Dangling description: "Mourning three spilled cups in a dark cloak, blinded to the two full cups standing upright behind you." The cups are not wearing the cloak.
- **TXT-073** · Major meanings stack adjectives until they mean nothing: "Resurrection, answering the higher calling, reckoning, and ultimate spiritual rebirth. Forgiving past missteps and stepping forward fully into your authentic cosmic vocation." "Humbling yet completely liberating." Strike "cosmic", "ultimate", "authentic", "profound", "sacred" and see what is left.
- **TXT-074** · Keywords are Title Case with ampersands ("Guilt & Shame", "Karmic Absolution", "Generative Abundance") and are lower-cased and injected into sentences by readers. Store them in lower case, plain words, no ampersands.
- **TXT-075** · `symbols` for majors are invented ("Cosmic Precipice", "Solar Spiral", "White Butterfly" for The Fool) and labelled traditional. Minors have none. See UX-009.
---

## 6. Consistency rules to apply everywhere

- **TXT-080 · One term per thing.** card (not plate, sheet); position (not seat, slot, house); reversed (not slipped, retrograde, in the dip) in interface text; turn over (not flip, reveal); reader (not oracle, seer) in interface text; history (not past readings); all cards (not compendium, case).
- **TXT-081 · Sentence case** for every label and heading. The CSS upper-cases buttons; the source strings should still be sentence case. Current mix: "1 Card", "Celtic Cross", "Allow reversals", "Past readings", "Choose a deck", "Shuffle & deal".
- **TXT-082 · No ampersands in labels.** "Shuffle & deal", "Reveal & read", "registered & activated", all four template-reader titles.
- **TXT-083 · One separator.** The app uses "•", "·", "—" and "/" for the same job.
- **TXT-084 · One style of quotation mark.** The interface uses curly quotes; Ruth's and Lyle's strings use straight ones, including around Lyle's slips.
- **TXT-085 · Never append punctuation to user text.** All seven readers add a comma, colon or full stop after the quoted question, producing `?".`, `?":` and `?."`.
- **TXT-086 · No fixed sentence may appear in every reading.** Openers, advice and closers for all seven readers are constants or pick from three. Each needs enough variants, keyed to something in the spread, that two readings in a row do not end the same way.
- **TXT-087 · Personality stays with the reader.** No reader's vocabulary in placeholders, buttons, headings or tooltips.

---

## 7. Outside the app

- **TXT-090 · README.** Describes four readers, port 8080 and a file tree that no longer matches. The prose is brochure copy: "The revered sacred mandala", "Living ambient HTML5 canvas overlay with organic candle flame flickering", "enabling seekers to write, validate, and register custom reader plugins in real time!". Rewrite as: what it is, how to run it (`npm start`, port 5173), where things live, how to add a reader.
- **TXT-091 · Page title.** "Astralis Tarot — The Candlelit Altar" → "Astralis — tarot readings". Add a one-sentence meta description; shared links currently unfurl with none.
- **TXT-092 · Names.** `package.json` is "night-window"; the server logs "Night window listening". One name.
- **TXT-093 · Code comments carry the mystic voice too** ("Sacred 108Hz", "528Hz Solfeggio frequency chime", "mystic filigree", "THE SACRED SPREAD ALTAR CANVAS"). Harmless to users, but they tell the next agent this is the house style. It should not be.
